tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After moving the current largest disk that is not yet in its final position onto its goal peg, treat the remaining disks as a smaller subproblem and solve it recursively. This ensures that each larger disk is placed correctly before handling the smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a largest disk that is not yet correctly placed can be moved to its goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing the largest disk, the solver continues moving other disks without recursively solving the remaining subproblem, leading to incorrect ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target. This preserves the required ordering.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous stack of disks while preserving their relative order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver tries to move a stack of two disks directly without first moving the top disk to the auxiliary peg, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer must consist of a single syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier reads the last parseable list in the response. Any surrounding text can be misinterpreted as part of the list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, after all reasoning is finished.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The answer includes explanatory text before the list, causing the parser to miss the move list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally replay each move from the initial state and confirm that the resulting arrangement matches the goal before submitting the list. This catches logical errors early.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move sequence, before final output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver outputs a move list that, when simulated, leaves a disk on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should contain only the move list; any additional text can be interpreted as part of the list and cause parsing errors. Keep the output minimal and clean.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the answer, especially at the end when presenting the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The answer contains a trailing comment after the list, which the parser treats as part of the list and fails.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the source peg's top disk matches the moving disk and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. This prevents illegal moves such as moving a non‑top disk or placing a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver attempts to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg, or places a larger disk onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere. This guarantees the size rule is never violated on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver moves a larger disk onto a peg where a smaller disk sits on top, violating the rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk on a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, unless you move the small disk away first. This prevents dead‑ends where a larger disk becomes blocked.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver moves a small disk onto the goal peg and never moves it away before trying to place a larger disk there, causing a dead end.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, relocate the smaller disks above it to any other peg before moving the larger disk. This frees the larger disk for a legal move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk you need to move is covered by smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver tries to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Only preserve disks that are already in final position on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When scanning the goal peg, keep a disk only if all larger disks are already present below it on that peg; otherwise, treat it as needing to be moved. This avoids disturbing disks that are already correctly placed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of planning, to decide which disks can be left untouched.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The solver moves a disk that is already correctly placed on the goal peg, breaking the final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation early or forgets to output any moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure you always output a non‑empty list of moves, even if it is just a placeholder that you later fill in.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation hit the token limit or stopped before finishing the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise, verify completeness before submitting, and avoid unnecessary commentary that consumes tokens.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the source peg's top before issuing a move.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always inspect the source peg and, if the desired disk is not on top, first move the blocking smaller disks elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg and never moves it away before a larger disk needs that peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only place small disks on the goal peg when they will stay there for the remainder of the solution, or move them away before moving a larger disk onto that peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model ignores the size rule that a larger disk may not rest on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, compare the moving disk size with the destination peg's top disk; only place onto larger or empty pegs.
